programme: FOSL1 (Fra-1, AP-1 family) together with the immediate-early factors NR4A3 and EGR2 and the MEF2-corepressor HDAC7 form a stress/hypoxia-inducible switch in myeloid and vascular cells: FOSL1 drives the matrix-protease programme (MMP1/2/9/13/14, elastin/FN1 turnover) and vascular adhesion genes; NR4A3 and EGR2 are the immediate-early factors that reset macrophage/microglial activation state (and, in the T-cell literature, drive anergy/tolerance); HDAC7 represses MEF2A/C/D and touches HIF1A, coupling the module to hypoxic adaptation. Together they read as an injury-triggered myeloid/vascular remodeling-and-resolution circuit rather than a single pathway.
role_in_a: In COPD this circuit operates in alveolar macrophages and airway neutrophils: EGR2 is required for tissue-specific alveolar macrophage imprinting (34797692), NR4A3/NR4A-family signaling modulates monocyte responses under hypercapnic/inflammatory lung stress (38474099) and links to a Nur77-associated anti-inflammatory axis (39902793), FOSL1/AP-1 marks a pathogenic neutrophil subset tied to neutrophilic inflammation (41998641), and the shared target set (MMP1/2/9/13/14, elastin) matches protease-driven emphysematous remodeling.
role_in_b: In ischemic stroke the same factors reappear in the cerebrovascular/neuroinflammatory response: EGR2 and NR4A3 are repeatedly picked out as hub regulators of post-ischemic repair — EGR2 via BNIP3L-mediated microglial mitophagy and exosomal neuroprotection (42016821, 40571783, 36208355), NR4A3 as a hub gene in ischemic-stroke regeneration and neuroprotection screens (40320842, 38505917, 34500302) — HDAC7 controls astrocyte reactivity through the cGAS/STING innate-immune axis after ischemia (41229730, 40867143, 40109665), and FOSL1 marks a shared endothelial metabolic-stress signature in cerebrovascular injury (37775708).
shared_axis: COPD produces chronic hypoxemia and systemic inflammation, both established drivers of cerebrovascular injury; if the two organs reuse the same myeloid/vascular stress-response module (FOSL1-NR4A3-EGR2-HDAC7) to convert hypoxic, inflamed tissue into a remodeling-and-repair state, that would explain why a blood/lung network comparison surfaces this set for both a chronic hypoxic lung disease and its downstream cerebrovascular consequence.
reasoning: No retrieved source states a COPD-stroke connection through these factors specifically, so this is not established; but all four carrying factors are independently and specifically placed in both diseases by distinct studies (alveolar macrophage/neutrophil biology for COPD, microglial/astrocyte/endothelial ischemic response for stroke), and the module is nameable from the factors' target sets alone, which is what 'supported' with 'strong' evidence requires. The counts (33/39, 32/39, 32/39, 31/39) also put all four well above the single-view cutoff, unlike TFCP2's isolated top score with no literature.
support: 41998641 (FOSL1 in COPD: pathogenic neutrophil subset marker); 37775708 (FOSL1 in stroke: shared endothelial metabolic-stress signature); 38474099 (NR4A3/NR4A family in lung inflammatory stress); 40320842, 38505917, 34500302 (NR4A3 as hub/regeneration regulator in ischemic stroke); 34797692 (EGR2 required for alveolar macrophage tissue imprinting); 42016821 (EGR2 in stroke via BNIP3L-mediated microglial mitophagy); 40571783, 36208355 (exosomal EGR2 neuroprotection in ischemia models); 39902793 (HDAC7/Nur77 axis in a lung inflammatory mouse model); 41229730 (HDAC7 knockout reduces astrocyte reactivity via IRF3/cGAS/STING after stroke); 40867143, 40109665 (HDAC7-linked neuroinflammation/hub-gene studies in ischemic stroke); 40497340 (general review touching HDAC biology in cardiovascular disease, not joint mechanistic evidence).
how_to_falsify: Compare alveolar macrophages from COPD lung tissue and microglia/peripheral monocytes from stroke patients (or matched hypoxia/LPS-challenged cell models of each): if FOSL1, NR4A3, EGR2 and HDAC7 knockdown fails to produce a coordinated shift in the shared target programme (MMP1/2/9/13/14, VCAM1/ICAM1, HIF1A-linked genes) in both cell types under comparable hypoxic/inflammatory stimulation, or if ChIP-seq shows the four factors do not co-occupy these targets in either cell type, the shared-module account is falsified.
caveats: Networks compare a blood-derived and a lung-derived transcriptomic network (39 patient-group comparisons drawn from only 4 independent cohort pairs, so replication depth is modest). Single-view exclusions (TCF4, NPAS2, CIITA, NKX2-1, ZHX3, ARID1B) included lung- and immune-identity factors that might have suggested a different, tissue-specific story had they generalized — they did not. Tissue-generic exclusions (CEBPB, FOXO1, KLF6, E2F2, STAT1, E2F1, IRF8, ERG, NR3C2, EZH2, SMAD3) stripped out the more obvious myeloid/endothelial/interferon regulators before ranking, so the remaining module is not simply restating 'these are macrophage/endothelial cells' — but it also means some plausible connective tissue (e.g. STAT1/IRF8 inflammatory signaling) was removed by design, not by evidence against it. Every citation here is disease-specific, not disease-pair-specific: no source discusses COPD and stroke jointly through these factors, so the cross-disease link is inferred from parallel single-disease biology plus the known clinical association between COPD and stroke risk, not from a documented shared mechanism.
